The petitioner, by way of this writ petition, seeks grant of following reliefs:
"i) Direct the Respondent No. 2 to form a board comprising not less than two registered medical practitioners and submit an opinion qua the medical termination of pregnancy of the Petitioner as warranted under Section 3(2)(b) of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971.; And ii) Further direct the Respondents No.1 & 2 to medically terminate the pregnancy of the Victim/Petitioner in view of the Explanation No. 2, Section 3(2) of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (as amended till date); And iii) Direct Respondent No. 1 to bear all the expenses necessary for the termination of the pregnancy of the Victim, her medicines, food etc; And This is a digitally signed order.

1 iv) Direct the Respondent No. 2 to preserve the terminal feotus for the purposes of DNA testing which would be required with reference to the criminal case which stands registered..."
2. Issue notice.
The learned ASC accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. The matter has been listed before this Court at 3:30 PM, as it was marked on an urgent mentioning before the Hon'ble Chief Justice.

4. The case, once again, relates to the urgent need for conducting the medical termination of pregnancy of a minor victim, aged about 14 years, who fell prey to sexual assault by her cousin brother, who is also a minor.
5. As on date, the victim is carrying pregnancy of about 28 weeks.

The Court is informed that the FIR in this case came to be registered on 08.08.2025, the victim was medically examined at Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, Delhi on 08.08.2025 and thereafter her ultrasound was conducted by AIIMS, Delhi on the same day, when she was found carrying pregnancy of about 27 weeks.

The minor child was produced before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) on 11.08.2025 and the following order was passed:
"...
When the child realized that her stomach is increasing, she shared it with her parental aunt.
Child was taken to Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, where the child came to know that she has pregnancy of 26-28 weeks.

Parental aunt M took the child S and her S**** (16 years) to PS Mehrauli, New Delhi,
FIR was registered, CCL S**** was produced before JJB and placed in observation Home.
MLC and 183 statement of S have been done and produced before CWC today is 26-28 weeks pregnant.
S has stated before the Bench that she does not wants to keep the pregnancy.
She wants to get the pregnancy terminated.
Father is not present today.
Her guardian/parental aunt M has also given consent for MTP.
I Probono is appointed as a Support Person in this case.
Child S wants to go with her Bua, but bua M does not want to take her to home in this situation.
S and her bua have given consent in writing for MTP.

approach Hon'ble Delhi High Court for further direction in this MTP case as child S pregnancy period has exceeded 24 weeks, and submit ATR in the case within a week.
7. IO/PSI Varsha is directed to provide the biological parents/father before CWC on or before NDOH...."

6. In terms of paragraph 4 of the order of CWC, the AIIMS, Delhi was directed to conduct medical termination of the pregnancy of the minor child, as per the medical assessment of the child and directions of this Court, and to submit a status report before the CWC.

Paragraph 6 of the order directs the Investigating Officer (I.O.) to take the case very seriously and approach this Court for further directions for the purpose of conducting medical termination of pregnancy, since the gestational period has exceeded 24 weeks.

7. The concerned I.O., who appears through video-conferencing, states that she had not received a proper copy of the order of CWC, and paragraph 4 of the order specifically was not received by her,
which she has received in This is a digitally signed order.

It has also been laid down by this Court in the aforesaid decisions that where a minor victim of sexual assault is found to be carrying a pregnancy of more than 24 weeks, and both she and her guardian consent to its termination, the Medical Board of the concerned hospital shall promptly conduct a medical assessment to determine whether it is safe to proceed with the termination.
This ensures that, when the victim approaches this Court for an order in this regard, no further time is lost in first directing the constitution of a Medical Board and awaiting its report.
Instead, an appropriate order can be passed forthwith, based on an already prepared medical assessment report of the minor victim.
10. Thus, it was incumbent upon the I.O. to have produced the victim child before the Medical Board of AIIMS, Delhi, and the concerned doctors, pursuant to the order passed by the CWC.

The Medical Board, in turn, ought to have assessed the minor victim on the following parameters:
(i) The exact gestational period of the pregnancy of the victim.
(ii) Whether the victim is physically fit to undergo MTP?
(iii) Whether the victim is mentally fit to undergo MTP?
(iv) Whether it will pose risk to the life of the victim in case of MTP?
11.

Unfortunately, a 14 years child, who is victim of sexual assault in unfortunate circumstances remains confined to Nirmal Chaya as the I.O. has still not taken her to the Hospital concerned for assessment, as required to be done by the medical board, for the purpose of passing final order by this Court.

However, at the same time, this Court also notes that the CWC also did not appropriately advise the I.O. in this regard, and in its direction no. 1, CWC directed the I.O. to approach this Court for seeking appropriate orders.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/08/2025 at 23:48:51 12.

Be that as it may, considering the emergent situation, this Court directs that the Medical Board,
which is constituted permanently for such purpose in AIIMS, Delhi and vide the notification extracted in paragraph 8 of this order, will ensure that the report regarding the medical assessment of the minor victim - for the purpose of conducting medical termination of pregnancy - is placed before this Court on 18.08.2025 before 2:00 PM.
